predecessors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
predecessors.text: the interior of Oman, which the page says was "controlled by the Seljuk Empire" in the 11th and 12th centuries

successors.name: Ya'rubid dynasty
successors.text: the interior of Oman: "In 1624 Nasir bin Murshid of the Ya'Aruba took over control of Oman"

ledger.x: 1154: the Nabhani come to power in Oman.
1475: Cliopatria's shape shrinks from 84 k to 4.4 k km2.
ledger.cp: Ibadi Imamate of Oman and Kingdom of Hormuz (page undated)

ledger.x: 1624: Nasir bin Murshid of the Ya'Aruba takes over Oman.

wars.name: Expulsion of the Seljuks from Oman
wars.outcome: Muhammed al-Fallah rose in 1151 and had taken control by 1154, when "the Seljuks were expelled".

wars.name: Portuguese capture of Muscat and the coast
wars.outcome: "In 1507 the Portuguese captured the coastal city of Muscat" and "gradually extended their control along the coast up to Sohar"; a Portuguese protectorate was imposed on the Nabhani ruler on 15 April 1515 (Nabhani page).

wars.name: Ya'rubid takeover of Oman
wars.outcome: Nasir bin Murshid, elected imam in 1624, took Nizwa, Rustaq and Nakhal; Julfar was taken from the Portuguese in 1633 and the fort of Sohar in 1643.

certainty.note: An interior dynasty of towns and forts with a shifting seat; no page gives a frontier, and the coast was held at times by Hormuz and the Portuguese.
